body:
Meaning of Software

Software consists of programs and associated instructions that direct computer hardware to perform tasks.

Unlike hardware, software does not refer to a physical component such as a keyboard or processor. Software provides the instructions that are executed using physical hardware.

For example, a keyboard is hardware, while a word-processing program is software. The keyboard allows text entry, and the word-processing program provides functions for preparing and editing documents.

Software: Programs and related instructions used to operate a computer or perform tasks through its hardware.

Main Types of Computer Software

At the introductory level, software is commonly grouped into system software and application software. Utility software is often discussed separately, although it is generally treated as a category of system software.

System Software

System software supports the operation of the computer and provides essential services needed by applications and users.

Important examples include:

  • Operating system: Manages hardware resources, files, running applications and user interaction.
  • Device driver: Allows the operating system and applications to communicate with a particular type of hardware device.
  • Utility software: Performs maintenance, protection or management tasks.

For example, a printer driver helps the computer communicate correctly with a supported printer. It is not itself the physical printer.

Application Software

Application software is designed to help users perform particular tasks.

Common applications include word processors, spreadsheet programs, presentation software, web browsers and media players.

A word processor helps prepare documents. A spreadsheet application helps organise data and perform calculations. A web browser helps users access and display web content.

Application software may be general-purpose or specialised for a particular activity.

  • General-purpose application: A word processor or spreadsheet used for many different tasks.
  • Special-purpose application: Software designed for a specific function, such as maintaining school examination records or managing billing.

Utility Software

Utility software helps maintain, manage, protect or organise a computer system.

Examples include antivirus programs, file-compression utilities, backup software and storage-management tools.

Utility software supports system operation or maintenance. It is not the same as an operating system, even though some utilities may be included with an operating system.

Comparison of Software Categories

CategoryMain purposeExamples
System softwareSupports computer operation and resource managementOperating system, device drivers
Application softwareHelps users perform tasksWord processor, browser, spreadsheet
Utility softwareMaintains, protects or manages the systemAntivirus, backup, compression utility

This table separates utilities for clarity. In the broader classification, utilities are commonly included under system software.

How Hardware and Software Work Together

When a user prepares a document, the word-processing application provides document-editing functions. The operating system manages resources, input and output services, and access to stored files. The CPU executes instructions, RAM holds active information, and hardware devices supply input and display output.

The operating system therefore forms an important software layer between applications and the computer's hardware.

Firmware

Firmware is software stored in non-volatile memory and used to control or initialise hardware functions.

For example, computer startup firmware helps initialise hardware and begin the process of loading the operating system. Firmware is software even though it is stored in an electronic component.

Hardware performs operations; software provides instructions. The operating system manages computer resources, while application software provides functions for users.

Prelims focus

  • Software consists of programs and instructions.
  • Operating systems are system software.
  • Word processors, spreadsheets and web browsers are application software.
  • Antivirus and backup programs are examples of utility software.
  • Device drivers support communication with hardware devices.
  • Trap: A web browser is application software, not an operating system.

[Sources: National Institute of Open Schooling, Data Entry Operations, Lesson 1, section 1.7, Software, including subsections 1.7.1 and 1.7.2, printed pp. 11–13; CBSE, Computer Science, Class XI, Unit 1, Chapter 2, Software Concepts; IBM, What Is an Operating System?, sections on operating-system functions and device management. Online sources consulted 14 November 2026.]

body:
Meaning of an Operating System

An Operating System (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware resources, supports application programs and provides ways for users to interact with the computer.

Without an appropriate operating system or equivalent system-control software, an ordinary general-purpose computer cannot provide the familiar environment needed to open applications, manage files and interact with devices.

Operating system: System software that manages computer resources and provides essential services and interfaces for applications and users.

Major Functions of an Operating System

Processor Management

The operating system coordinates the use of CPU time by running programs. When several applications are active, the operating system helps arrange when their instructions are executed.

This supports multitasking, in which a computer can make progress on multiple tasks during overlapping periods.

Multitasking does not necessarily mean that a separate physical CPU is required for every application. The operating system can coordinate execution across available processing resources.

Memory Management

The operating system manages the use of working memory. It makes memory available to running applications and coordinates its use so that programs can operate reliably.

When an application is opened, the operating system helps load the required program and data into working memory.

File Management

The operating system allows users and applications to create, open, save, copy, move, rename and delete files, subject to applicable permissions.

A file is a named collection of stored information. A folder or directory is used to organise files and, where supported, other folders.

File management helps users locate and organise information stored on a computer.

Device Management

The operating system coordinates communication with devices such as keyboards, mice, monitors, printers and storage drives.

Device drivers help the operating system communicate with particular hardware devices.

User Interface

The operating system provides or supports an interface through which users can interact with the computer.

Two important interface styles are:

  • Graphical User Interface (GUI): Uses visual elements such as windows, icons, menus and pointers. Users commonly interact through a mouse, keyboard or touchscreen.
  • Command-Line Interface (CLI): Allows users to enter text commands to request operations.

GUI and CLI describe methods of interaction. They are not separate physical types of computer hardware, and the same operating system may support both.

Security and User Management

The operating system may manage user accounts, authentication and permissions. These functions help determine which users or applications can access particular files and system resources.

Examples of Operating Systems

Operating systems are used in desktop computers, laptops, smartphones and many other computing devices.

Computing environmentOperating-system examplesTypical use
Desktop or laptopWindows, macOS, Linux-based systemsDocuments, browsing and general computing
Smartphone or tabletAndroid, iOSMobile applications and device operation

These examples identify operating-system families rather than particular product versions. The distinction is between the system software managing the device and the applications running on it.

What Happens When a Computer Starts?

The process of starting a computer and preparing its operating environment is commonly called booting.

  1. The computer receives power and its startup firmware begins operating.
  2. The firmware performs essential initialisation and starts the process of loading the operating system.
  3. The operating system is loaded from storage into working memory and begins managing the computer's resources.
  4. The computer becomes ready for supported user interaction and application use.

The exact startup process differs among devices, but the essential distinction is that startup firmware begins the process and the operating system subsequently provides the main operating environment.

Practical Example: Using Multiple Applications

Consider a student preparing notes on a laptop while listening to an educational audio recording.

The word processor and media player are application software. The operating system manages the applications' access to memory, processing resources and devices.

The keyboard provides text input, the monitor displays the document, and the speakers provide audio output. The CPU executes instructions, RAM supports active operations, and persistent storage retains successfully saved documents.

When the student saves the notes, the operating system helps arrange the file-writing operation. The saved document remains available after normal shutdown.

Putting the Computer System Together

The central relationship is straightforward. Hardware supplies physical computing components. Software provides instructions. The CPU performs processing, RAM supports active work, and storage devices retain saved files. Input and output devices connect computer operations with users, while the operating system manages resources and supports applications.

The historical development of computers is commonly remembered through vacuum tubes in the first generation, transistors in the second, integrated circuits in the third, microprocessors in the fourth and AI-oriented computing in the conventional fifth-generation classification.

Important Distinctions for Objective Examinations

  • CPU and operating system: The CPU is hardware; the operating system is software.
  • System software and application software: System software manages or supports computer operation; application software performs tasks for users.
  • RAM and persistent storage: RAM holds active working information; HDDs and SSDs retain saved files.
  • Input and output: Input devices supply information; output devices present results.
  • GUI and CLI: Both are interaction methods, not alternatives to the basic purpose of an operating system.

Prelims focus

  • An operating system is system software.
  • Its functions include processor management, memory management, file management and device management.
  • GUI stands for Graphical User Interface.
  • CLI stands for Command-Line Interface.
  • Booting prepares a computer by starting and loading its operating environment.
  • Windows, macOS, Linux-based systems, Android and iOS are operating-system examples.
  • Trap: Multitasking is an operating-system capability; it does not require one separate CPU for every running application.

[Sources: IBM, What Is an Operating System?, sections on resource allocation, file management, device management, user interfaces and operating-system components; National Institute of Open Schooling, Data Entry Operations, Lesson 1, section 1.7.1, System Software; CBSE, Installation Technician: Computing and Peripherals, Class XI, Chapter 4, Introduction to Operating System; CBSE, Computer Science, Class XI, Unit 1, Chapters 1 and 2, Computer Fundamentals and Software Concepts; Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University, Fundamentals of Computers & Information Technology, 2020 edition, Unit 1, section 1.4. Online sources consulted 14 November 2026.]
